newsitem.title: USA: Cohen to block promotion for Khobar Towers commander.
newsitem.headline: Cohen to block promotion for Khobar Towers commander.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen will punish the commander of U.S. operations in Saudi Arabia for failure to tighten security at the Khobar Towers barracks before last year's deadly truck bombing, U.S. networks reported on Wednesday.

Cohen has decided to recommend to President Bill Clinton that Brig. Gen. Terryl Schwalier, who had overall command of U.S. air operations in Saudi Arabia, be denied a promotion to two-star general, NBC and ABC reported.
Nineteen airmen died in the truck bombing at the Khobar Towers building on June 25, 1996.
After long deliberation, Cohen had decided that Schwalier should be held accountable for not doing more to prevent the attack, the networks said.

The Air Force said in January it had delayed the promotion to major general for Schwalier pending final action in the controversy. Before the delay, Schwalier had been nominated for promotion by Clinton and confirmed by the Senate.

The Pentagon had no comment on the network reports, which followed Monday's resignation of Gen. Ronald Fogleman, the U.S. Air Force chief of staff, apparently in a protest against the possible blaming of subordinates for security lapses at the Saudi Arabian facility.
Fogleman said he was acting to "defuse the perceived confrontation" between him and Cohen over the truck bombing.
Cohen was to decide this week whether to hold one or more commanders responsible for failing to take steps that might have thwarted the attack.

A Pentagon task force last year faulted Air Force field commanders for not paying adequate attention to security around the Khobar barracks, concluding that they "did not take all measures possible to protect the forces at Khobar Towers."
The task force, headed by retired Army Gen. Wayne Downing, recommended that punitive action be considered by the chain of command -- ultimately by the defence secretary.
Fogleman wanted Schwalier to be given his second general's star.
